items.headline: Virtual biotech company puts thousands of AI scientist agents to work on drug discovery
items.excerpt: Stanford researchers built a virtual biotech staffed by tens of thousands of AI agents that mined thousands of clinical trials and proposed a cancer therapy later pursued independently by a major pharma company.

items.headline: How a simple game of 20 questions could help make AI fit for the future
items.excerpt: University of Bristol researchers show image classifiers can be trained cheaply using simple binary yes/no queries inspired by the game 20 Questions, instead of million-dollar GPU runs.

items.headline: Smart, self-healing packaging uses AI to detect food spoilage in real time
items.excerpt: Kyushu University researchers propose a framework combining sensors, self-healing materials and AI models that read freshness signals to flag spoilage in real time.

items.headline: Manuscripts-turned AI agents can now 'talk' to each other and make new discoveries
items.excerpt: Stanford's Paper2Agent converts scientific manuscripts into interactive agents that answer questions about their own methods and collaborate with other paper agents to generate new findings.

items.headline: AI expands mathematics: A new frontier of reverse problem generation for computational AI
items.excerpt: Chiba University's Hiroshi Kera explains how 'reverse problem generation' — building equations from known solutions — supplies the training data that lets machine learning accelerate computational algebra.

items.headline: AI still isn't as good at recognizing objects as people are, new test shows
items.excerpt: A new study finds vision models collapse on distorted images where humans still read overall shape, evidence that machine perception does not work the way human object perception does.

items.headline: Which million-dollar math problem could AI solve next?
items.excerpt: After an OpenAI model offered a possible Navier-Stokes solution, mathematicians debate which remaining Millennium Prize problem an AI system is most likely to crack — and what counts as a proof.

items.headline: Powerful new AI model will map the moon's surface in more detail than ever, NASA and IBM scientists say
items.excerpt: IBM and NASA built the Lunar Foundation Model, an open geospatial AI trained on decades of lunar orbiter data to map the moon's surface at unprecedented detail.

items.headline: Earth From Orbit Is Unpredictable and Messy. Could 'Liquid' AI Clear the View?
items.excerpt: Earth observation data is noisy and irregular; researchers argue liquid neural networks, which adapt their dynamics at inference time, could make satellite monitoring far more robust.

items.headline: Chess Reveals Differences Between Human and AI Strategies
items.excerpt: A complexity analysis of chess games finds grandmasters steer toward less complex positions faster than engines do, exposing different strategies for balancing short- and long-term prospects.

items.headline: Using AI to plan for climate variability in renewable energy systems
items.excerpt: A new AI approach models decades of weather variability to show how batteries and hydrogen storage can be sized to keep renewable grids reliable.

items.headline: USA Rare Earth, Pasqal and Riven Test Quantum Machine Learning for Rare Earth Separation
items.excerpt: USA Rare Earth is working with Pasqal and Riven to test quantum machine learning for extractant selection, aiming at the chemistry bottleneck in rare earth separation.

items.headline: AI models need more data about biology, and OpenAI is paying to create it
items.excerpt: The OpenAI Foundation is funding 'Data for Public Health' to generate the missing biological datasets that current models cannot learn from.

items.headline: Can AI fix health care? In the chaos of emergency rooms, the technology comes up short
items.excerpt: A close look at AI scribes and decision tools in emergency departments finds the technology falls well short of the claims made for it in real clinical workflows.

items.headline: ARPA-H to invest $62 million to develop FDA-authorized AI to help treat heart failure
items.excerpt: ARPA-H will commit $62.7 million to build autonomous AI agents that direct heart failure treatment, with the goal of FDA authorization.

items.headline: Teaching future scientists to interrogate AI tools for scientific discovery
items.excerpt: University of Washington students stress-tested Ai2's AutoDiscovery agent, finding it surfaces promising scientific leads while making human judgment and validation more important, not less.

items.headline: Bypassing inference bottlenecks: Accelerating complex AI search with Retrieve-for-Train
items.excerpt: Google Research describes Retrieve-for-Train, a method that removes the inference bottleneck in large-scale AI search pipelines used for combinatorial scientific and engineering problems.

items.headline: Hypothesis-Driven Autonomous Materials Synthesis with Multimodal LLM Agents
items.excerpt: Self-driving labs usually optimize synthesis with black-box optimizers; this preprint replaces that layer with multimodal LLM agents that form and test explicit hypotheses about why a synthesis works.

items.headline: Securing quantum error correction against misleading advice from AI agents
items.excerpt: The authors show how an attacker with influence over an AI adviser could push harmful quantum error-correction updates, and propose safeguards for AI-assisted decoding.

items.headline: Evaluation of methods for AlphaFold-based integrative modeling
items.excerpt: A systematic benchmark of methods that inject experimental restraints into AlphaFold, testing how well data-guided structure prediction actually works for integrative modeling.

items.headline: Ourotide: decoding the hierarchical peptide recognition for generative design
items.excerpt: Ourotide models peptide binding as a hierarchical recognition process rather than a structural intermediate, and uses that decomposition to drive generative peptide design.

items.headline: HeartVar: An LLM-Assisted Tool for Clinical Classification of Variants in Cardiovascular Disease Cohorts
items.excerpt: HeartVar uses an LLM to assemble and weigh the 28 ACMG criteria behind clinical DNA variant classification, attacking the manual curation bottleneck in rare disease workflows.

items.headline: Consolidating Antibody Discovery Data with an AI Platform
items.excerpt: FairJourney Biologics describes moving scattered multi-site antibody discovery data onto a single AI platform so models can actually learn from years of wet-lab campaigns.

items.headline: AI Accelerates Biomanufacturing from Discovery to Translation
items.excerpt: A survey of how machine learning models are being wired into bioprocess development, from cell line selection to process control, to shorten discovery-to-translation timelines.
